thread:
marco: FinServ asked if we can run a 1-week POC showing streaming responses, strict JSON schema enforcement, and a CRM lookup that never exposes their CRM to Redwood IPs. Also need guidance on reserved capacity pricing and SSO/SOC2 docs.

trina: I can build a tiny streaming demo + a final validated JSON output. Will need to know whether they prefer short-lived session tokens or a service account for the connector.

liam: For the CRM proxy: suggest a small customer-side connector (runs in their VPC) so CRM sees only their IPs. For hosted POC we can also show a local proxy in the demo. If they insist on static Redwood IPs we can talk Dedicated NAT ranges but that triggers network review.

anya: On schema enforcement: we support post-generation validation hooks. We can auto-retry with a constrained prompt or return a structured error. We can also surface validation failures in audit logs for the POC.

marco: Pricing ask: they want a reserved option for predictable latency. Tina, can you sketch three options: hosted demo (credits), 1-month reserved pilot, 6-month commit? Include estimated token burn if they share qps/avg seq.

sec-bot: Attaching docs we can share: SOC2 summary, SAML/OIDC SSO guide, KMS integration notes, audit-log export (90d). I will DM links to the thread.

trina: I'll push a repo with a short README showing how to run the proxy locally, a python streaming snippet, and an example of enabling runtime schema validation. ETA tomorrow AM.

liam: I'll prepare two network flows to show during the call: connector-in-vpc and hosted-with-short-lived-creds. Also note HSM/KMS differences for Private vs Dedicated.

marco: Action items: trina repo + README; liam provide network options + KMS note; anya add schema validation sample and retry policy; sec-bot post links. I'll propose two demo times to the customer.

trina: Quick snippet we'll include:
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="REDACTED")
for chunk in client.generate_stream(model="rwd-small-1", prompt="Lookup customer 42 and return JSON:"):
    print(chunk.text, end="")
# final call with schema enforcement
resp = client.generate(model="rwd-small-1", prompt="Produce JSON {\"id\":int,\"status\":string}", output_schema='{"type":"object","properties":{"id":{"type":"integer"},"status":{"type":"string"}},"required":["id","status"]}', validate_schema=True)
print(resp.json)
```

marco: Thanks team. Keep it concise for exec demo.
